blogs.title: When 'Angioedema' Doesn't Respond to Epinephrine: Recognizing Myositis-Induced Neck Swelling
blogs.description: Explore the diagnostic pitfalls when a patient presents with severe neck swelling and dysphagia that mimics classic histaminergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema. This post analyzes why standard treatments fail in cases of dermatomyositis-associated pseudo-angioedema, emphasizing the pathophysiology of muscle inflammation causing soft tissue edema versus vascular permeability changes.

blogs.title: The CK Clue: Why Every Patient with Unexplained Edema Needs a Creatine Kinase Level
blogs.description: Discuss the critical role of the creatine kinase (CK) level as a rapid, low-cost screening tool in the emergency department. Using this case where CK was >16,000 U/L despite subtle weakness, we examine how overlooking basic muscle enzymes can delay life-saving immunosuppression and lead to unnecessary workups for infectious deep neck space infections.

blogs.title: Beyond Gottron's Papules: Decoding Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis and Its Unique Phenotype
blogs.description: Delve into the specific serological profile of anti-SAE1 antibody-positive dermatomyositis. This post contrasts the classic cutaneous signs often missing in early presentations (like the absence of heliotrope rash here) with the distinct risks associated with SAE1 positivity, including high rates of dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, and the rarity of subcutaneous edema.

blogs.title: Aspiration vs. Infection: Navigating Airway Management in Severe Pharyngeal Myositis
blogs.description: Analyze the management tension between treating suspected deep neck infection versus managing neuromuscular dysphagia. We review how video fluoroscopic studies revealed severe aspiration due to pharyngeal weakness rather than obstruction, guiding decisions on nasogastric feeding, airway protection strategies, and avoiding unnecessary surgical interventions.

blogs.title: Malignancy Screening in High-Risk Dermatomyositis: A Protocol for the Clinician
blogs.description: Outline a systematic approach to paraneoplastic screening in adult-onset dermatomyositis. Focusing on this patient's risk stratification (male sex, dysphagia, SAE1 status), we discuss current IMACS guidelines for tumor detection, including the utility of PET/CT scans versus traditional tumor markers and the necessity of age-appropriate endoscopic surveillance.
